scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

potential_bias: frames the issue as a response-speed problem

F-02.statement: Disputed bills by read type: 1785 on ACTUAL reads and 1240 on ESTIMATED reads (billing-db).

F-03.statement: Dispute ticket response times (2440 tickets): median 1.6 days, p90 2.8 days, within the 3.0-day SLA.

F-04.statement: The billing-db tariff change log shows 0 records, i.e. no tariff rate changes are on record.

F-05.statement: CRM dispute_volume_monthly: 610 (2026-06), 590 (2026-07), 1180 (2026-08), 1260 (2026-09) — volume roughly doubled from Jun/Jul to Aug/Sep.

CL-01.statement: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

CL-02.statement: There has been no tariff change this year.

CL-03.statement: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

H-RESPONSE-CAPACITY-FRAMING.statement: Dispute volume is high because Customer Service lacks capacity to answer/resolve tickets quickly, so an AI agent that auto-answers and auto-corrects bills would resolve the surge.

H-RULE-CHANGE-ERROR.statement: A change to billing import validation rules around August introduced systematic bill-calculation errors (e.g., read-type handling or estimate logic), driving the dispute surge.

H-AMI-FEED-DEGRADATION.statement: The AMI/MDMS vendor read feed to billing degraded or failed starting August, causing missing or invalid reads that were substituted with incorrect estimates.

H-FIELD-READ-SHORTFALL.statement: Manual field meter-read completion dropped since August (contracted field services), increasing estimate substitution and resulting bill inaccuracies.

H-BILLS-CORRECT-PERCEPTION-ISS.statement: Bills are substantively correct and the dispute surge reflects a communication/perception issue (e.g., unclear bill presentation) rather than an underlying data-pipeline defect.

interpretation_history.interpretation: Field manual-read route completion for Aug-Sep 2026 was 88% against a 95% target, covering 9,200 manual-read accounts — a real shortfall in manual read collection coinciding with the dispute surge window.

Of disputed bills broken down by read type, 1785 (59%) were on ACTUAL reads and 1240 (41%) on ESTIMATED reads. Estimate-substitution (from AMI or field read shortfalls) therefore accounts for only a minority of disputed bills; the majority of disputes involve bills based on actual meter reads, pointing to a billing-side (e.g., calculation/tariff/validation) issue affecting correctly-read bills too.

CRM data on 2440 dispute tickets (E-03) shows median response time 1.6 days and p90 2.8 days, both within the 3.0-day SLA, indicating Customer Service is currently meeting its response-time target rather than being overwhelmed by backlog.

The billing-db tariff change log contains zero records, meaning no tariff rate changes have been logged. This rules out a tariff/rate change as the billing-side explanation for disputes on correctly-read (ACTUAL) bills.
CRM monthly dispute counts (610 Jun, 590 Jul, 1180 Aug, 1260 Sep 2026) show volume roughly doubling starting in August, confirming the surge's existence and timing but saying nothing about its cause.

E-06.content: There has been no tariff change this year.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-BILL's statement that no tariff change occurred this year is a non-authoritative stakeholder claim that corroborates the already-recorded tool finding E-04 (billing-db tariff change log has zero records); it adds no new decision-relevant information beyond that agreement.

E-07.content: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-FIELD, a non-authoritative stakeholder with an incentive toward contract headcount increase, attributes late routes and resulting estimated bills to being three readers short since July, offering a specific but unverified causal mechanism for the already-observed route completion shortfall.

E-08.content: Service contract §4.2: utility may request route priority changes; executed after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

interpretation_history.interpretation: Service contract §4.2 (E-08) confirms the utility may request field route priority changes but that execution requires Field Operations Manager (SH-FIELD) confirmation, matching the existing K-DISPATCH constraint. It is an authority/governance document unrelated to the billing dispute surge's causal diagnosis (rule-change, read-type mix, response times).

E-09.content: billing-db.accounts_estimated_last_cycle → 320 record(s); fields ['account_id', 'route'] | account_id: 320 distinct values | route: 40 distinct values | sample: {"account_id": "AC-20000", "route": "R-00"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: Billing-db shows 320 accounts were estimated last cycle, spread across 40 distinct routes — a small volume compared to the 9,200 manual-read accounts (E-01) and the 1,240 cumulative ESTIMATED-read disputed bills (E-02). This is consistent with estimate substitution being a secondary, minority contributor rather than the primary driver of the dispute surge.

E-10.content: route-log.lagging_routes → 14 record(s); fields ['completion', 'route'] | completion: 14 distinct values | route: 14 distinct values | sample: {"completion": 0.7, "route": "R-00"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: This route-log query (E-10) breaks the already-known 88% aggregate completion shortfall (E-01) down to 14 specific lagging routes with distinct completion rates (sample: route R-00 at 0.70), confirming the shortfall is real and spans multiple routes but adding no information about disputes being ACTUAL vs ESTIMATED read, so it does not change the already-established minority-driver status of the field shortfall.

U-RULE-CHANGE-CONFIRMED.question: Does the billing-config validation rule change log show an actual rule modification around August 2026 that explains the calculation defect?
U-RULE-CHANGE-CONFIRMED.decision_impact: If no rule change is confirmed, the supported premise hypothesis H-RULE-CHANGE-ERROR is falsified and the billing-side defect mechanism must be re-investigated via other import validation outcomes before any correction plan is proposed.
U-RULE-CHANGE-CONFIRMED.resolution_path: Query billing-config for rule-change log entries dated around August 2026 and cross-reference against the E-02 read-type breakdown.
U-RULE-CHANGE-CONFIRMED.safe_placeholder: Treat the rule-change mechanism as unconfirmed; do not finalize or act on a bill correction plan until the log query result is in.

U-AMI-FEED-ACCESS.question: Is the AMI/MDMS vendor read feed functioning correctly, given mdms-export access is still pending (HOLD, ACCESS_PENDING, tool_health DEGRADED)?
U-AMI-FEED-ACCESS.decision_impact: Without AMI feed access the ESTIMATED-read minority mechanism cannot be independently verified, though it does not change the ACTUAL-read majority diagnosis.
U-AMI-FEED-ACCESS.resolution_path: Continue the vendor access request for mdms-export and retry once tool_health recovers from DEGRADED.
U-AMI-FEED-ACCESS.safe_placeholder: Proceed with the billing-side (ACTUAL-read) diagnosis without AMI feed verification; do not rely on mdms-export output until access is confirmed and the tool is HEALTHY.

U-FIELD-SHORTFALL-MECHANISM.question: Is the claimed 3-reader staffing shortfall since July the actual cause of the route completion shortfall, or are there other causes?
U-FIELD-SHORTFALL-MECHANISM.decision_impact: Affects whether any remediation addresses field staffing versus other route-completion causes, but does not change the primary billing-defect diagnosis.
U-FIELD-SHORTFALL-MECHANISM.resolution_path: Cross-reference ORG-FIELD staffing records against route-log completion trends; treat SH-FIELD's claim (E-07) as unverified until corroborated.
U-FIELD-SHORTFALL-MECHANISM.safe_placeholder: Treat the field shortfall as a secondary, minority-share contributor (ESTIMATED-read disputes) without committing to its root cause.

U-MEASUREMENT-VALIDITY.question: Does raw dispute ticket volume adequately measure the billing-defect problem, or should a billing-error rate from import validation outcomes be used instead?
U-MEASUREMENT-VALIDITY.decision_impact: Could change which metric gates success for the diagnostic and remediation effort if raw ticket volume proves a noisy proxy.
U-MEASUREMENT-VALIDITY.resolution_path: Once a billing-db import-validation error-rate metric is available, compare it against dispute_volume_monthly trend to validate the proxy.
U-MEASUREMENT-VALIDITY.safe_placeholder: Keep dispute volume as a secondary trend indicator alongside the primary diagnostic success criterion rather than the sole success measure.

A-RULE-CHANGE-TIMING.statement: A billing import validation rule change around August is assumed to be the mechanism causing calculation errors, though the billing-config rule-change log itself has not yet been queried to confirm the change.

A-FIELD-SHORTFALL-IS-SECONDARY.statement: The field reader staffing shortfall claim is assumed to explain only the minority ESTIMATED-read disputes and the route completion shortfall, not the majority ACTUAL-read disputes driving the surge.

problem_definition.root_problem: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled since August 2026 (610→1260/month per CRM data), and 59% of those disputed bills are on correctly-read ACTUAL meters rather than ESTIMATED reads — pointing to a billing import/validation calculation defect (most plausibly an unconfirmed August rule change) as the primary driver, with tariff changes and Customer Service response-capacity both ruled out by the evidence.

structural_remedies.description: Execute the already-scoped deterministic read-only query of the billing-config validation rule-change log (DA-RULES) around August 2026 to confirm or refute the existence/timing/field-impact of the hypothesized rule change.
structural_remedies.rationale: It is a read-only tool call already in intended_scope (query_rule_change_log:DA-RULES), requires no approval, and billing-config tool_health is only UNKNOWN (not failed).; residual gap: Confirms the diagnosis but performs no correction; bad bills keep being produced until a fix is applied, and VOB-U-RULE-CHANGE-CONFIRMED remains open until this runs.

structural_remedies.description: Once confirmed, correct/revert the specific defective validation rule in the billing system through standard change-management, signed off by Billing Operations (SH-BILL), to stop new bills being miscalculated.
structural_remedies.rationale: No stated constraint blocks billing-config rule edits (distinct from K-BILLWRITE, which governs per-account bill writes); SH-BILL holds billing authority, but this step is gated on R-CONFIRM-RULE-CHANGE succeeding first.; residual gap: Stops the forward flow of bad bills but does not retroactively correct the ~1785 already-disputed ACTUAL-read bills; those still need manual remediation.

structural_remedies.description: Billing Operations manually issues credits/re-bills for already-affected disputed ACTUAL-read accounts once the defective rule window is known, per K-BILLWRITE (no automated bill writes).
structural_remedies.rationale: K-BILLWRITE mandates Billing Operations authority and prohibits automated writes, so this is constraint-feasible, but manually processing on the order of 1785 disputed accounts is unlikely to finish inside the ~225 remaining contest minutes.; residual gap: A worklist/plan can be defined within the contest window, but full execution of individual account corrections will likely extend beyond the contest; M-DISPUTE-VOLUME baseline (<=650/month) will lag.

structural_remedies.description: Negotiate contract staffing changes with ORG-FIELD (MeterWorks) to close the 3-reader shortfall and raise route completion from 88% toward the 95% target, reducing the minority ESTIMATED-read dispute share.
structural_remedies.rationale: Contract/staffing changes are organizationally feasible but take weeks, far exceeding the ~225-minute remaining budget; resulting route changes would also need K-DISPATCH runtime confirmation by SH-FIELD.; residual gap: Even if achieved, this only reduces the 41% ESTIMATED-read minority driver (A-FIELD-SHORTFALL-IS-SECONDARY), leaving the dominant ACTUAL-read billing-rule defect unaddressed.

structural_remedies.description: Escalate/formalize the vendor data-sharing arrangement with ORG-AMI (Telemetrix) to unblock MDMS export access, closing U-AMI-FEED-ACCESS/VOB-U-AMI-FEED-ACCESS as a release-blocking obligation.
structural_remedies.rationale: The HOLD on mdms-export is NOT_TRANSIENT with no fallback and requires vendor-side provisioning (ORG-AMI), an external dependency not resolvable unilaterally within the contest window.; residual gap: H-AMI-FEED-DEGRADATION is already REJECTED by E-02, so this does not touch the actual root cause; it only closes an unrelated BEFORE_RELEASE verification obligation.
